newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natural gas price climbs at AECO.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natural gas price climbs at AECO.

text.p: Spot natural gas prices at the key AECO trading hub in Alberta jumped from Tuesday's levels as temperatures failed to climb to forecast levels.
However, most Canadian prices were down from last week.
Spot gas at the AECO storage hub was talked at C$2.60/2.65 per gigajoule, up sharply from C$2.35/2.40 in Tuesday trade. AECO gas fetched C$2.68/2.70 on January 29.
Gas for March delivery was quoted at C$2.20/2.25, up about 10 cents from Tuesday.
"The weather is moving all the front months up," said a Calgary-based trader.

Environment Canada said temperatures in southern Alberta were forecast to climb above freezing and continue rising throughout the week. But temperatures have stubbornly stayed just below 0 Celsius (32 Fahrenheit).
The trader said utilities had been taking in gas in the Alberta market to feed the unexpected heating demand but there were fears that prices would fall if the warmer weather materialized.

At the borders, gas for export at Niagara, Ontario was quoted at US$3.00/3.05 per million British thermal units, down up to 40 cents from last week. Gas at Sumas, Wash. was discussed in the mid-$2.10s down about 20 cents.
